original_value: Underwater cracks in concrete structures are often difficult to detect due to their complexity of the service environment. With numerical and experimental analysis of concrete beams immersed in water, an active monitoring system, based on a cement-based piezoelectric intelligent module array (CPIMA), was developed to locate and quantify the underwater cracks. Time reversal (TR) of the stress wave field is accomplished to focus on the crack area through the concrete beam specimen by the system. First, a piezoelectric actuator is applied to emit the initial propagating wave, which can be reflected, attenuated, and diffracted by the crack, transmitted through water filled in the crack, as well as diffracted by the coarse aggregates. To extract the damage waveforms associated with the crack and analyze the robust time-reversal invariance under the high-order multiple scattering effect, a pair of homogeneous and heterogeneous forward finite element (FE) models is established. Then, the damage waveforms are time-reversed and re-propagated in the inverse numerical model, where an optimal refocusing is achieved on the crack that behaves as an acoustic source. Finally, the damage area is obtained in the form of the stacked energy distribution of each time step. The focus results are represented by cloud images and compared with root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) values. Numerical simulation and experiments show that this method can identify and quantify underwater cracks effectively.

result.paraphrase: Underwater cracks in concrete structures are often hard to detect because the service environment is complex. Based on numerical and experimental studies of concrete beams immersed in water, an active monitoring system using a cement-based piezoelectric intelligent module array (CPIMA) was developed to locate and quantify underwater cracks. The system uses time reversal (TR) of the stress wave field to focus on the crack region within the concrete beam specimen. First, a piezoelectric actuator emits an initial propagating wave that may be reflected, attenuated, and diffracted by the crack, transmitted through water in the crack, and diffracted by coarse aggregates. To extract crack-related damage waveforms and examine robust time-reversal invariance under high-order multiple scattering, a pair of homogeneous and heterogeneous forward finite element (FE) models is built. The damage waveforms are then time-reversed and re-propagated in the inverse numerical model, where optimal refocusing is achieved on the crack, which acts as an acoustic source. Finally, the damaged area is derived as the stacked energy distribution at each time step. The focusing results are shown as cloud images and compared with root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) values. Numerical simulations and experiments demonstrate that this method can effectively identify and quantify underwater cracks.
